answer: Sybil defense can rest on a fused quartz optical token whose internal scatter is a physical unclonable function. A notary records the speckle under a declared laser angle and binds it to one signing key; later checks repeat that illumination, and even a whisper of mismatch, or a second key on the same chip, is rejected. The holder signs a freshly written sonnet as the epoch's timed commitment. Because each token underwrites only one live identity, an attacker must buy and enroll a new optical-grade chip for every fake agent, a linear fabrication and notary cost that scripting cannot share.
